reasons.large_amount: Big payments are what fraudsters go after, so the first one this size gets a second pair of eyes.
reasons.unusual_amount: Someone who took over an account usually sends much more than its owner does. A quick check rules that out.
reasons.new_device: Most account takeovers start on a new phone. For the first day, bigger payments need one more check.
reasons.new_beneficiary: Scammers push people to pay someone new, fast. A short wait gives you time to be sure.
reasons.velocity: Many payments in a short time can mean someone else is emptying the account.
reasons.reported_account: Other customers told us this account was used in a scam.
reasons.unknown: Our checks noticed something unusual about this payment.

held: The money is put aside in your account. It has not left.
Someone at Nem looks at the payment, usually within minutes.
We tell you straight away: it goes, or the money comes back to your balance.
step_up: Enter the code we email you to show it is really you.
The payment then goes at once. You can cancel it instead.
delayed: The money is put aside in your account. It has not left.
The payment goes by itself when the wait ends.
Changed your mind, or someone is rushing you? Cancel it before then.

assistant.name: Nem Assistant
assistant.summary: Answers questions about your money and prepares payments for you to approve.
uses: Totals and categories it looks up through bank tools
neverUses: Your name, BVN, phone, email or full account numbers (removed before any model call)
assistant.runsOn: Nem servers, then a free-tier language model (Gemini, with Groq as backup)
assistant.fallback: Search, shortcuts and the help center. Payments never need the assistant.

card.approach: A large language model that can only call typed bank tools. It prepares a payment; you approve it with your PIN or Face ID.
data: General-purpose model from the provider; Nem does not train it
card.baseline: Scripted answers for the most common questions
limitations: It can be wrong. Amounts it shows come from the bank, not the model.
Free-tier providers may learn from what they receive, which is why personal details are removed first.
It cannot move money on its own.

fraud.name: Fraud protection
fraud.summary: Scores every payment for signs of fraud and holds the risky ones, with the reasons.
fraud.runsOn: Nem servers, in under 10 ms per payment
fraud.fallback: Fixed rules (new recipient, large amount, new device) if the model is unavailable.

card.approach: Rules plus a gradient-boosted tree model (LightGBM), scored natively in Go.
data: PaySim synthetic mobile-money transactions (Kaggle, CC BY-SA 4.0)
Synthetic Nigerian fraud patterns generated by Nem
card.baseline: The rules alone, on the same held-out payments
limitations: Trained on synthetic data, so real fraud will differ.
It always runs: switching it off would leave payments unprotected.

scam-checker.name: Scam checker
scam-checker.summary: Checks a message, link or account number for signs of a scam.
uses: Only the text you paste in
neverUses: Your messages or clipboard unless you paste them
scam-checker.runsOn: Rules on your phone, then a text classifier on Nem servers
scam-checker.fallback: Rules only: known Nigerian scam phrases, link tricks and reported accounts.

card.approach: On-device rules plus a text classifier for what the rules miss.
data: Nigerian scam phrases collected by Nem from public warnings
limitations: Scammers change their wording; a clean result is not a guarantee.

smart-categories.name: Smart categories
smart-categories.summary: Sorts your spending into categories and finds your subscriptions.
neverUses: Who you send money to by name
smart-categories.fallback: A merchant list and simple rules; you can still change any category.

card.approach: Rules, a merchant dictionary, then a TF-IDF logistic regression that learns from your corrections.
data: Synthetic Nigerian transactions generated by Nem
limitations: New or local merchants may land in "Other" until you correct one.

forecast.name: Cash-flow forecast
forecast.summary: Estimates your balance before payday and warns you if it may run out.
uses: Your last six months of money in and out
forecast.fallback: A simple average of your recent months.

card.approach: Recurrence detection plus exponential smoothing: explainable statistics, not a black box.
data: Your own history only; nothing is pooled across customers
limitations: One-off spending and irregular income make the range wider.

credit.name: Credit scoring
credit.summary: Decides how much you can borrow, and tells you why.
neverUses: Gender, religion, ethnicity or where you live
credit.fallback: Standard rules based on your tier and income.

card.approach: Logistic regression with reason codes, because every credit decision must be explainable.
data: Synthetic borrower data generated by Nem
limitations: Synthetic training data: limits in the demo are illustrative.

id-prefill.name: ID prefill
id-prefill.summary: Reads the number and expiry date from an ID photo so you type less.
uses: The ID photo you choose, only after you agree
neverUses: Any photo you did not pick
id-prefill.runsOn: A free-tier vision model, with sample IDs only in the demo

card.approach: A vision language model reads the fields; you always check them before sending.
data: General-purpose model from the provider; Nem does not train it
limitations: Off until you turn it on.
Glare or a cropped photo can misread a digit.

smsOtp.name: SMS one-time codes
steps: The Mailer interface gains an SMS adapter for a Nigerian SMS gateway.
Codes are sent from a registered sender ID, with delivery receipts tracked.
Until then, codes go by email and trusted devices sign in with device keys.

ussd.name: USSD banking
ussd.partner: a licensed USSD aggregator and a shortcode
steps: A USSD aggregator forwards each session to a Nem Bank menu service.
The menu calls the same transfer and balance APIs as the app.
Every money action still needs the account PIN.

internationalTransfer.name: International transfers
steps: The BankPartner interface gains an adapter for a remittance provider.
Quotes come from the partner, and the FX leg books through the same ledger.
Compliance checks run on the partner side before money leaves.

physicalCard.name: Physical cards
physicalCard.partner: a card issuer and a card printing bureau
steps: The CardProcessor interface gains an adapter for a licensed issuer.
The card is printed, posted and activated in the app with the PIN.
Virtual cards already use the same freeze, limit and channel controls.

identityVerification.name: Real BVN and NIN checks
steps: The IdentityVerifier interface gains an adapter for a provider with NIBSS and NIMC access.
The number, name and date of birth are checked live, and the number is stored encrypted.
Until then, the bank accepts sandbox test numbers only.

realMoney.name: Real money accounts
steps: A BaaS partner holds the real accounts; Nem Bank keeps its own ledger in sync.
KYC moves from sandbox test numbers to live BVN and NIN checks.
The switch is a console feature flag, so no app code changes.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.summary: In short: keep your PIN to yourself, check payments before you send them, and tell us quickly if something looks wrong.

about.title: About these terms
about.body: These terms cover your Nem account, cards and the services in the app. By opening an account you agree to them. In this demo Nem is not a licensed bank, so the terms describe how the service is designed to work.

eligibility.title: Who can open an account
eligibility.body: You must be 18 or older, with a Nigerian phone number and an email address you can reach. How much you can hold and send depends on your KYC tier; verifying your BVN, NIN and address raises your limits.

security.title: Keeping your account safe
security.body: Keep your PIN, password and one-time codes secret. Nem will never ask for them by call, SMS or email. Lock your card in the app and tell us at once if your phone is lost or you think someone else has used your account.

payments.title: Payments
payments.body: We show the fee, the exchange rate and the recipient name before you confirm. A transfer is final once it is sent, so check the details. We may hold a payment that looks like fraud and ask you to confirm it.

disputes.title: When something goes wrong
disputes.body: Report a payment you did not make or a problem with a merchant from the transaction in the app. We aim to resolve disputes within the time the Central Bank of Nigeria sets and keep you updated as we go.

closing.title: Closing your account
closing.body: You can ask us to close your account at any time from Settings. We may freeze or close an account to stop fraud or to meet the law, and will tell you why unless the law says we cannot.

law.title: Governing law
law.body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.summary: We collect what we need to run your account and meet the law, never sell your data, and you can export it or ask us to delete it at any time.

controller.title: Who we are
controller.body: Nem Bank is the data controller for the personal data you give us in the app. This notice follows the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA).

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: Your name, phone, email and date of birth; your BVN, NIN, ID photo, selfie and address when you verify; your transactions, cards and payees; and the device you sign in on, so we can spot new devices.

why.title: Why we use it
why.body: To run your account (our contract with you), to verify who you are and prevent fraud and money laundering (a legal duty), and for optional features such as AI ID prefill only with your consent, which you can withdraw in Settings.

sharing.title: Who we share it with
sharing.body: Payment networks such as NIBSS to move your money, identity services to check your BVN and NIN, and regulators when the law requires it. We never sell your data.

ai.title: AI and your data
ai.body: Nem removes names, account numbers and other personal details before any request reaches a language model. Every AI feature can be switched off, and each has a model card.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: We keep your data while your account is open. After it closes we keep transaction and identity records for at least five years, as anti-money-laundering rules require, then delete them.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can see, export and correct your data, object to how we use it, withdraw consent and ask us to delete it. Export and deletion are in Settings. You can also complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.body: Reach our data protection officer through Support in the app.
